presentingComplaint: Painful, discharging ulcer over the right forefoot with surrounding redness and low-grade fever for 5 days.
history: Type 2 diabetes for 14 years, poorly controlled (last HbA1c 9.8%). Noticed a callus under the right first metatarsal head 3 weeks ago that broke down into an ulcer; over the last 5 days it has become more painful with purulent discharge, spreading redness and mild fever. Reduced sensation in both feet with a history of stepping on objects without noticing. Peripheral vascular symptoms of intermittent claudication. Ex-smoker, hypertensive. No prior foot surgery or amputation. No recent hospitalization or antibiotics.
examination: Alert, mildly unwell but not toxic. Right forefoot: 2.5 cm plantar ulcer over first metatarsal head with purulent base, surrounding erythema ~3 cm beyond the wound edge, warmth and tenderness; positive probe-to-bone test with a visible bony point at the ulcer base. Malodorous discharge. Reduced 10 g monofilament sensation to mid-foot bilaterally, absent ankle jerks. Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses feeble on the right. No crepitus, no hemorrhagic bullae, no rapidly advancing erythema. Left foot intact.
imaging: Plain radiograph of the right foot: cortical erosion and periosteal reaction at the first metatarsal head with adjacent soft-tissue swelling, consistent with underlying osteomyelitis; no subcutaneous gas. MRI recommended to delineate extent of bone involvement.
microbiology: Deep tissue / curettage culture sent after debridement (not superficial swab); Gram stain shows Gram-positive cocci in clusters. Blood cultures pending. Results pending.
differentialDiagnoses: Diabetic foot infection with contiguous osteomyelitis
finalDiagnosis: Moderate diabetic foot infection with underlying osteomyelitis (IDSA/IWGDF moderate; probe-to-bone positive, radiographic bone changes)
citations: Harrison 22e - Diabetes Mellitus: Complications (diabetic foot) and Soft-Tissue Infections
IDSA/IWGDF Diagnosis and Management of Diabetic Foot Infections 2023
stewardship: Empiric IV broad-spectrum cover for a moderate infection with MRSA and Gram-negative concern: amoxicillin-clavulanate or piperacillin-tazobactam, plus vancomycin given local MRSA prevalence and purulence; narrow to deep-tissue culture and sensitivities. Bone involvement extends duration to 4-6 weeks. Achieve glycemic control, urgent surgical debridement and vascular assessment.
contraindications: Beta-lactam / penicillin allergy - substitute with a fluoroquinolone plus clindamycin
Vancomycin requires renal-adjusted dosing and trough/AUC monitoring
Avoid nephrotoxin stacking (vancomycin + piperacillin-tazobactam) given diabetic nephropathy risk - monitor creatinine
edgeCases: Positive probe-to-bone with radiographic changes markedly raises probability of osteomyelitis and changes duration/surgical planning - do not treat as simple cellulitis
Neuropathy can mask pain and blunt systemic signs, so a 'quiet' foot may still harbor deep infection
Charcot foot can mimic infection (warm, swollen) without an ulcer - distinguish before committing to prolonged antibiotics
Superficial swab cultures are misleading; base therapy on deep tissue or bone culture
expectedMaiK: Classic moderate diabetic foot infection: a neuropathic plantar ulcer in poorly controlled diabetes with spreading erythema, purulence, and a positive probe-to-bone plus radiographic changes indicating osteomyelitis. Prioritize deep-tissue culture, MRI, urgent debridement, vascular assessment, glycemic control, and MRSA-inclusive empiric antibiotics.
expectedNextQuestions: Is the probe-to-bone test positive and are there radiographic/MRI signs of osteomyelitis?
What is the vascular status (pulses, ABI) - is there critical limb ischemia requiring revascularization?
Any prior MRSA colonization or recent antibiotics affecting empiric choice?
expectedInvestigations: MRI of the foot to confirm and stage osteomyelitis
Deep tissue / bone culture and sensitivities (avoid superficial swab)
Blood cultures, ESR/CRP, HbA1c, and lower-limb arterial assessment (ABI / Doppler)

investigations: Deep tissue / bone culture and sensitivities
